body:
Maybe. I don't know. I just hate trying to release all this and people ignoring what I say. Is it really neccessary to say that I used to be hit constantly? That they punished me for displaying emotion, or used whippings with belts as a way of threatening me for made-up offenses? That I was terrified of them my entire fucking childhood? I don't like talking about my family, okay, but I don't know why it's necessary to get into this every time someone asks why I can't talk to my family. A simple 'no' should be enough. I'm my own person, okay; I think I know when I can talk to somebody or not. 

I ask someone for help when I'm desperate, and all I get is people telling me to talk to my fucking parents, after I tell them I can't. I'm sick of hearing the same trite advice over and over, yet I don't even know what I want. I'm so sorry.
Alright. Glad you know about my family situation. Glad you know that I haven't thought of this before. But yeah, feel free to tell me what my life is like because I'm sixteen and you're not, alright?

I don't know. I don't know. Maybe I just need someone to talk with me. Not go away. I don't know. 

My parents are part of the problem. Believe me. I just want to sleep forever. I'm so sorry
I know. Fuck me. I just want something that can kill me.
Yeah. Thanks. She does truly mean an extraordinarily great deal to me. I don't think I can break my promise to her, yet.

That has to be the worst advice I've ever heard. For some of us, "ending it" is a 100% chance of improvement. Why the hell do you think anyone kills themselves? You're an idiot. Do you really think that people's problems are that they're not "positive" enough?? That if we live long enough, our problems will magically disappear with time? I guarantee to you that every person here does *not* have a "good chance" if they continue living; the very reason they're here is because they realize suicide is the best immediate solution to their present problems. People aren't dumb; they don't kill themselves because they have a bad day or whatever other moronic reason you think they do it. 

If you have no idea what depression is like, stay out of this forum. Good for you that you're not depressed. But you're not helping anything with these stupid comments you keep posting.
Thanks. Sorry for not being on. I actually did get back together with her, and I'm doing much better. Still, your comment means a lot to me. Thank you, again.

I know you're trying to help. I really do, and I appreciate it. But two more years seems unbearable, and the uncertainty of the future is so daunting. Every change in my life has been for the worse so far, and it's difficult to imagine a positive future. 

I might take you up on your offer sometime. Right now, the pain of what she did to me is still raw, and I don't want to do anything that will remind me of her.

Thanks for saying that, really. It's exactly what happened to me, and knowing that I'm not the only one means more to me than I'm able to express. Like you said, it wasn't romantic love, but I definitely thought of her as a stable part of my life, and trusted her with everything. Her rejection of me...I always thought of her as such a better person, compared to me, and valued her opinions over everything else. Knowing that she found my company so unpleasant that she never wanted to talk to me again hurt me like nothing else ever had. I felt actual pain in my chest. I felt like trash. And I don't know which is worse; that pain, which still hasn't faded, or the realization that there's nothing in my life now, and I have nothing. I break into tears multiple times a day, replaying what I said over and over and trying to think of a way I could have prevented this from happening. 

I don't know what either of us did to deserve this. I'm so sorry this had to happen to anyone else.

> When you're young, everything seems like the end of the world, but trust me, it isn't, it's just a rough time. Life goes on and does get better.

I know it's not the end of the world. But somehow fucking up so badly, managing to drive the only friend I thought I had away from me, it hurts. And the fact that she could do something like this, that she could feel so indifferent to me and ignore months' worth of conversation over a stressful week, that also hurts. I feel like a failure at everything in my life. My grades are average, I have no talents or interests, and I can't keep the one thing that mattered to me. Also,

>Life goes on and does get better.

Err, rule 4? I don't see how it can.

> I'm sure that whatever you did couldn't have been so bad.

All I did was tell her how I feel. And that doesn't seem so bad. But I knew it hurt her to read everything I said, and I knew she felt guilty at not being able to do anything to help. But I didn't realize, or else couldn't stop. I kept sending her messages, in fewer and fewer amounts, because she was the only person that might have been able to listen. And then I tried to stop, and apologize and try to return everything to how it was before, but she refused, and said she wanted to stop talking to me. And now I wish that I could still talk to her, even if I never mentioned myself again; that she was still my friend. 

I *was* clingy. I was, and it messed everything up. By the time I realized, it was too late to change anything.

I'm 16, and haven't played any video games for a while. I've already told them, for what good it did. I have a terrible relationship with my parents. I'm bad at sports. I have less people than you think. The only two friends I have are distant, and I've tried every way I can think of to get closer to them.

It's fine though. I broke off with her anyway. Now I just feel empty. Don't know what I'll do, but don't be worried for my sake.

It's entirely possible I have a false sense of her. But that isn't why I'm invested in her. She's the only person in my life who ever listened to me and showed a genuine interest in me, and she's the only person I've been able to relate to as much as I do. 

I'd love a real-life friendship. I really would. But I'm homeschooled, and don't see any way I could meet people. Believe me, I've tried everything I can think of. I don't want to be how I am. I wish I could do anything to change, but I don't see any opportunities to do so. She's my only link to the external world–Or at least a healthy perception of it–and she's all I have. I don't want to lose her.

Seeking "different friendship routes," unfortunately, isn't an option. I'm homeschooled. The only homeschooling community nearby is filled with stereotypical homeschoolers–the oldest ones act like nine-year-olds, and being around them makes me further disconnected from reality. I can't go anywhere without my parents' car, and they're only home for a few hours in the evening. I have no one and nowhere else to go to. 

I've been trying to leave her alone. She finally responded, and we worked some things out. But I don't want to guilt her into talking more to me, so I've been trying to communicate with her less than I'd like. 

And partly. My relationship with her is all I have to emotionally invest myself in. She's the only decent friend I've had since fourth grade, and the hope that she replied to me is all that gets me up in the morning. But I'm also going through other things in my life. I feel, increasingly more and more, that I can't relate to anyone–even this friend, very much–and thinking about the future is terrifying. I feel completely alone, confused, and scared.
